gazulus_opening.speaker: Johannes Gazulus
gazulus_opening.text: Gazulus finishes a line before rising. He leaves a strip of paper across the page, weighs it down with a brass instrument, and offers you the chair by the window. 'The Senate has read your appeal, Majesty. I have been asked to convey its profound concern.' He waits until the clerk has withdrawn. 'Now we may discuss what that concern might bear.'

cotrugli_opening.speaker: Benedetto Cotrugli
cotrugli_opening.text: Cotrugli is arguing with a man whose sleeves smell of wet rope. He settles the dispute by counting out three coins, then turns to you. 'A damaged cask. According to the porter it was damaged before he touched it; according to the owner it became damaged upon being touched. They will both be happy enough by supper. Have you come with a letter for the Republic, or a cargo that needs finding?'

gazulus_official_refusal.speaker: Johannes Gazulus
gazulus_official_refusal.text: 'We have fields in Konavle which their owners cannot safely reach. The Senate will not promise you a war while it is occupied with its own.' Gazulus lays down the refusal with the seal towards you. 'I cannot change the answer by making it less plain. But a merchant's lawful cargo is another matter. If you intend to speak with Benedetto, do so before his ship leaves.'

cotrugli_private_offer.speaker: Benedetto Cotrugli
cotrugli_private_offer.text: 'I cannot pledge Ragusa,' Cotrugli says. 'You would be buying something I do not own.' He takes a clean sheet and rules it into columns. 'I can ask which merchants have goods, which captains will take them, and what they require against the danger. There will be names on this paper. If any man fails you, you will at least know which name to curse.'

cargo_agreed.speaker: Benedetto Cotrugli
cargo_agreed.text: Cotrugli reads the terms aloud, including the part everyone hoped he would overlook. Gazulus corrects one word concerning the Republic; Cotrugli corrects the freight. At last the merchant folds the paper. 'The captain will receive his instructions. Pray for a fair passage, Majesty. I have allowed for several difficulties, but I should prefer not to pay for all of them.'

chair_gazulus.speaker: Johannes Gazulus
chair_gazulus.text: This month Gazulus has the chair. He has moved the accounts aside to make room for his instructions. Cotrugli, standing beside the window, points out that the accounts were also instructions. Gazulus invites you to sit before they pursue the distinction.

chair_cotrugli.speaker: Benedetto Cotrugli
chair_cotrugli.text: Cotrugli has taken the chair and brought the table closer to the light. Gazulus remains within reach of the correspondence. 'A temporary arrangement,' the scholar says. 'Naturally,' replies Cotrugli. 'Almost everything profitable is.'

food_denial_gazulus.speaker: Johannes Gazulus
food_denial_gazulus.text: 'The Republic cannot imperil its relations with the Sultan by supplying Constantinople.' Gazulus gives the sentence its full weight, then puts the sealed answer aside. Your payment is entered in a merchant's account. 'There is, however, a captain leaving for Albania. Your harbourmaster should make him welcome if his business brings him further east.'

food_denial_cotrugli.speaker: Benedetto Cotrugli
food_denial_cotrugli.text: 'Ragusa must decline,' Cotrugli says, signing the receipt for your money. He notices your expression. 'That is the Republic's answer. This is a purchase. An Albanian captain will attend to it, and I strongly advise against asking him why his cook speaks like my cousin.'

food_albanian_arrival.speaker: The harbourmaster
food_albanian_arrival.text: A vessel from Albania unloads five hundred measures of provisions. Its captain is unusually anxious to establish that he has never met a Ragusan councillor. The harbourmaster hears him out while the porters count the sacks. At the bottom of the manifest, in a familiar hand, someone has written: 'Please acknowledge safe receipt. Privately.'

war_contract_gazulus.speaker: Johannes Gazulus
war_contract_gazulus.text: Gazulus reads the terms back to you before sealing them. 'You are sending men whom your own walls may need. I shall not insult you by pretending the decision is small.' He checks the rolls against the agreement. Cotrugli has already summoned the clerk who will arrange their passage. For once, neither man has anything to add.

war_contract_cotrugli.speaker: Benedetto Cotrugli
war_contract_cotrugli.text: Cotrugli turns the agreement so you can read it in the light. 'The service, the reward and the return passage are all here. I prefer an argument before a signature.' When you have signed, he sets the troop rolls beside the contract. Gazulus asks for a second copy to be made for the captain.

war_day90_victory.speaker: Ragusan dispatch
war_day90_victory.text: The dispatch carries good news and an order for payment. Your contingent has helped Ragusa prevail. The promised ten thousand gold is credited to your treasury; the soldiers are still abroad, awaiting the passage home. Gazulus's letter names the men commended by their officers. Cotrugli's addition is shorter: 'Their return has been arranged. Expect them in a fortnight.'

war_day90_defeat.speaker: Ragusan dispatch
war_day90_defeat.text: The first page describes positions abandoned and orders overtaken by events. The second gives the names. Your contingent has not brought Ragusa the victory it sought. The returning men remain abroad while passage is arranged. 'A fortnight,' Cotrugli writes. Below it, Gazulus has added: 'Their officers will give you a fuller account when they reach you.'

war_day104_victory_return.speaker: The returning contingent
war_day104_victory_return.text: The transports enter the harbour with your men aboard. Their officers come ashore first, carrying the rolls and the Ragusan letters of commendation. The soldiers have been paid and have opinions about the wine. By evening they are back on the City's strength, telling their comrades how the fighting went.

war_day104_defeat_return.speaker: The returning contingent
war_day104_defeat_return.text: Your men come ashore without a welcome procession. Their captain presents the rolls, then asks to speak where he cannot be overheard. There will be time to examine the orders and to decide where the fault lay. For now, those who have returned are entered back on the City's strength.
